newsitem.title: UK: Construction firms see rise in Q1 output - report.
newsitem.headline: Construction firms see rise in Q1 output - report.

text.p: More companies in the UK construction sector have reported a rise in 1997 first quarter output compared with the previous quarter in continued evidence of a sustained upturn, said an industry survey on Friday.

The Building Employers Confederation's latest quarterly trends survey showed a positive balance of 37 percent of companies reporting a rise in output compared with the fourth quarter of 1996. There was also evidence from industry respondants that tender prices were up along with new work enquiries.
One third of those surveyed said they were working at or close to full capacity, showing little change on the preivous quarter.
On the industry's forecast for the rest of the year, a balance of 53 percent of companies expected output to rise, with larger firms the most optimistic.

The strongest sectors were private industrial building and private commercial projects. But housing repair and maintenance work fell back and enquiries for private new housing also dropped despite a strong housing market.
The BEC chairman Sir Martin Laing said he was confident the industry would hit its target of a three percent rise in volumes for 1997, sustaining its position through to the millennium.
